title: Three Years and One Short Margin
subtitle: 出版传媒 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 出版传媒（人与社会·科学与技术·信息与出版）
meta: 主题语境：出版传媒（人与社会·科学与技术·信息与出版）　|　核心词汇：format　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 format 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 the printer ① set a format that no editor in the press would have named, and he said the setting was the whole of the spring. The ② format, meaning the layout itself and not the text, ran three years and stayed unnamed in the book; a format, he said, is the only thing in a press that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ format in that press had the same short margin beside it, and the ④ format at the far shelf, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A format, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the printer said the naming is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the format was the whole of the matter, meaning the file type and not the layout. The ⑥ format, meaning the file type and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; format, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both a layout and a file type. He said the file type is the part they remember.

By 1975 the ⑦ format had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short margin. The ⑧ format of the whole thing, the printer wrote in April, was one press and three years of naming; format, he said, is either the one at the far shelf or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ format I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1977 and is still described as the quietest in the press. A ⑩ format, my mother said in 1979, is the only one that improves by being named; every format, she said, is a file type that has agreed to look like a layout. She said the file type was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 版式；排版（指印刷所里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 版式（指那一种本身，与正文相对）
C. 固定搭配：set a format 设定一种版式
D. n. 版式（指留给孩子们的那一种）
E. n. 版式（抽象总称，指一家印刷所的排版之事）
F. n. 版式（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一种）
G. n. （计算机文件的）格式；类型（指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 文件格式（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: set a format that no editor in the press would have named
The format, meaning the layout itself and not the text
the format at the far shelf

answers.why: set a format 意为“设定一种版式”，1968 年那位印刷工设定了一种印刷所里没有一位编辑肯说出名字的版式。
format 意为“版式”，指那一种本身而不是正文，它经过了三年而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
format 意为“版式”，指印刷所里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一道矮矮的页边。
format 意为“版式”，指留给孩子们的那一种，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
format 意为“文件格式、类型”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这种文件格式就是那件事的全部。
format 意为“文件格式”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那一种版式，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
format 意为“版式”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一种，到 1975 年这一种成了计划里的一行。
format 意为“版式”，印刷工四月写道，整件事的排版之事是一家印刷所和三年的说出名字。
format 意为“版式”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一种，1977 年结束了，至今仍被说成印刷所里最安静的一种。
format 为抽象总称，母亲 1979 年说，一种版式是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。
